# design stage notes — issue #1944

## What I read (initial pass)

- core/pipeline/runner.sh (lines 1-100, 871-1006, 1698-2663, 2813-2857): main() structure, traps, signal trap, abort trap, _runner_end_on_abort, _render_pipeline_end, _pipeline_status_glyph, _runner_render_open_items
- scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh: full file — abort word vocabulary (6 words), sentinel mechanics, first-wins
- scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh: full file — _route_resolve_knob pattern (template > env > manifest > constant)
- scripts/lib/proc-group.sh: full file — zbuild_pg_kill (refuses own group), _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill (TERM+grace+KILL)
- core/pipeline/template.sh: template_stage_router_timeout and related accessors, _TPL_SOURCE_FILE pattern
- docs/adr/ADR-025-abort-propagation.md: full — abort word list, Enforced by section
- docs/adr/ADR-054-stage-contract.md: full — §6a (disposition words incl. timed_out), §7 (always-run/release/persist), §9 (per-stage router knobs); timed_out IS already a disposition word in §6a
- config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt: ADR-054 IS in baseline (line 53); ADR-025 is NOT (has Enforced by)
- core/state/resume.sh: get_resume_recommendation — timed_out falls through to `*) → fresh_start` (NO resume)
- core/pipeline/state_helpers.sh: _set_pipeline_status — no status validation, just sets the field
- tests/unit/abort-propagation-test.sh: A8 loop (line 86) enumerates 6 abort words → wrong by omission
- tests/unit/runner-pipeline-end-test.sh: T9 STATUSES (lines 155-161) enumerates 5 pipeline statuses → wrong by omission
- tests/unit/run-open-items-test.sh: O3 loop (line 102) tests specific reasons; O9 (line 189) asserts EXACTLY "5" runner loop-ending lines → will break if timed_out arm added to _runner_end_on_abort (count becomes 6) → supersedes
- tests/integration/resume-state-machine-test.sh: no hardcoded status count, just specific transition tests; not wrong by omission

## What I read (refinement pass)

- docs/adr/ADR-006-resume-contract.md lines 140-149: exhaustive pipeline status enum table (in_progress, complete, interrupted, aborted, failed, preflight_failed) — WRONG BY OMISSION when timed_out added
- docs/adr/ADR-015-stage-io-capture.md lines 819-823: exhaustive pipeline status → glyph/color table — WRONG BY OMISSION when timed_out added
- scripts/lib/run-open-items.sh lines 79-116: run_end_words() case statement — timed_out falls through to catch-all; needs explicit case added
- core/pipeline/runner.sh _runner_abort_trap (2487-2559): sets pipeline status "interrupted" on exit; does NOT check abort word — the timed_out arm needs to be in _runner_end_on_abort (called from dispatch points), AND the signal trap (line 2652) overwrites _RUNNER_ABORT_REASON with the signal word, which must be amended to read from sentinel post-arm
- core/pipeline/runner.sh _runner_render_open_items (line 996): gate is `failed|interrupted|aborted` — needs timed_out added
- tests/integration/always-run-exit-paths-test.sh: tests specific exit paths for always-run stages; does NOT enumerate all cases exhaustively; not wrong by omission
- tests/integration/pipeline-resume-test.sh: tests specific get_resume_recommendation cases; does NOT enumerate all manual_resume_only cases; not wrong by omission

## Key architectural findings

1. **No existing run-level limit**: only per-stage router.timeout_s knobs. This is entirely new.

2. **Abort word vocabulary** (ADR-025 #1850): sigint | sigterm | cycle_abort | llm_unavailable | llm_rate_limited | scope_too_large. Adding timed_out grows this set.

3. **zbuild_pg_kill in proc-group.sh REFUSES ITS OWN GROUP** — the watchdog runs in the runner's PG, so it cannot use zbuild_pg_kill to kill that PG. Watchdog must use raw kill commands instead.

4. **Watchdog design**: background subshell captures _RUNNER_RUN_PGID at arm time (before & ), then sleeps, writes timed_out to sentinel, kills the runner PG with TERM + 10s + KILL. Does NOT source proc-group.sh — uses raw kill/sleep.

5. **Sentinel first-wins**: _zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel is no-op if a word is already recorded. Watchdog writes timed_out BEFORE sending TERM → runner's SIGTERM trap calls _zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel("sigterm") which is a no-op → _RUNNER_ABORT_REASON must be read from the sentinel after arming (not from the signal word) for timed_out to propagate correctly.

6. **resume.sh get_resume_recommendation** falls through to `*) → fresh_start` for unknown statuses. A timed_out pipeline-state would NOT be resumable unless resume.sh is updated to handle `timed_out → manual_resume_only`.

7. **timed_out disposition** already exists in disposition.sh for STAGE-level use. This change adds it as a PIPELINE-level abort word and pipeline status.

8. **O9 count assertion**: run-open-items-test.sh O9 asserts EXACTLY 5 runner "loop-ending lines." Adding a timed_out arm to _runner_end_on_abort adds a 6th matching line → O9 is SUPERSEDED.

9. **_render_pipeline_end has a catch-all** (line 947: `*) word="$status"`) so `timed_out` would render as "Pipeline timed_out:" without a specific case — this is acceptable. But _pipeline_status_glyph and _pipeline_status_color need explicit timed_out → fail cases (currently `*` gives `?` glyph / yellow color).

10. **proc-group.sh is NOT sourced by runner.sh** — only by route.sh. Watchdog uses inline kill commands (no zbuild_pg_kill needed, since it's killing its own PG which zbuild_pg_kill refuses anyway).

11. **ADR-006 and ADR-015 missed in previous pass** — both enumerate the pipeline status set exhaustively and are wrong by omission when timed_out is added. Added to scope in refinement pass.

## Scope — confirmed exhaustive

### Wrong by omission (closed-set enumerations that grow):
- tests/unit/abort-propagation-test.sh (A8 abort word loop, line 86)
- tests/unit/runner-pipeline-end-test.sh (T9 STATUSES array, lines 155-161)
- tests/unit/run-open-items-test.sh (O3 reason loop, line 102)
- tests/golden/pipeline-end/ — two new golden files needed
- docs/adr/ADR-006-resume-contract.md (pipeline status enum table, lines 140-149) [NEW]
- docs/adr/ADR-015-stage-io-capture.md (glyph/color table, lines 819-823) [NEW]

### Superseded by behavior change:
- tests/unit/run-open-items-test.sh O9: asserts count=5, becomes 6 when timed_out arm added to _runner_end_on_abort

### ADR baseline:
- config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt — remove ADR-054-stage-contract.md when ## Enforced by added

## WIRING

Primary: core/pipeline/runner.sh — calls _runner_resolve_run_limit_s(), arms watchdog, modifies _runner_abort_trap and _runner_end_on_abort for timed_out
Secondary: core/pipeline/template.sh — provides template_max_run_s() which _runner_resolve_run_limit_s() calls

330	+A run has no upper bound on its lifetime without this section. A long-running stage or a
331	+deadlock between dispatches can run indefinitely. CI job limits are platform-specific; the
332	+engine must enforce its own ceiling.
333	+
334	+**§11 — run-level wall-clock limit.**
335	+
336	+- The engine resolves a single per-run limit (`_runner_resolve_run_limit_s` in
337	+  `scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh`) using this precedence order:
338	+  1. Template `max_run_s:` key (top-level YAML) — read by `template_max_run_s()` in
339	+     `core/pipeline/template.sh`.
340	+  2. `ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S` environment variable.
341	+  3. Engine default: **20700 seconds** (≈ 5 h 45 m).
342	+  A non-integer or non-positive value in either source (1) or (2) is a misconfigured
343	+  disposition: the runner exits 1 before any stage runs.
344	+- The limit source is never platform-specific. No reference to `GITHUB_ACTIONS`, `CI`,
345	+  `TRAVIS`, `CIRCLECI`, `RUNNER_OS`, or similar variables appears in the limit-resolution
346	+  code.
347	+- A background watchdog subshell is armed in `main()` after the traps are installed. It
348	+  sleeps for the resolved limit, writes `timed_out` to the abort sentinel
349	+  (`_zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel timed_out`), then sends SIGTERM to the runner's process
350	+  group. After a 10-second grace, it sends SIGKILL to the runner's child processes (not
351	+  the runner itself), allowing the runner's deferred SIGTERM trap to fire and exit with
352	+  rc=1. The EXIT trap kills the watchdog on clean exit.
353	+- A timed-out run ends with pipeline status `timed_out` (ADR-006), a `pipeline.end`
354	+  event carrying `status=timed_out`, the in-flight stage name, and `limit_s`. The
355	+  `always_run` stages (release, persist) still execute via the EXIT trap's
356	+  `_runner_dispatch_always_run` call.
357	+- A resumed run receives a fresh watchdog armed from its own wall-clock start — the
358	+  original run's elapsed time is not carried forward. `get_resume_recommendation`
359	+  returns `manual_resume_only` for `timed_out` state.
360	+
361	+## Enforced by
362	+
363	+- §11: limit resolution precedence (template > env > 20700), misconfigured validation →
364	+  `tests/unit/run-limit-precedence-test.sh`
365	+- §11: run ends `timed_out`, `pipeline.end` event carries stage + `limit_s`, watchdog
366	+  fires between dispatches, TERM-ignoring stage reaped within TERM+10 s, always-run
367	+  stages execute →
368	+  `tests/integration/run-timed-out-test.sh`
369	+- §11: watchdog reaped on clean exit, pipeline status unchanged after normal run →
370	+  `tests/unit/run-watchdog-clean-exit-test.sh`
371	+- §11: resumed run gets fresh watchdog; `get_resume_recommendation(timed_out)` =
372	+  `manual_resume_only` → `tests/integration/resume-after-run-timeout-test.sh`

ADR-054 §4 makes exit codes binary everywhere, the engine's own paths included. This ADR's two layers carried the abort *as* an rc (130, then 143, and later 6, 9 and 10 joined), and every reader mapped those numbers its own way — `cycle_orchestrator_run` collapsed a nested `cycle_abort` into `config_invalid` (#1860). The layers stay; what they carry changes.
 
-- **An abort is recorded once, as a word:** `sigint`, `sigterm`, `cycle_abort`, `llm_unavailable`, `llm_rate_limited` or `scope_too_large`. It is held in the process (`_ZB_ABORT_REASON`) and written into the sentinel `${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal`, which still crosses subshells and env scrubs (ADR-024). The first recorded abort wins. An empty sentinel reads as `sigint`.
+- **An abort is recorded once, as a word:** `sigint`, `sigterm`, `cycle_abort`, `llm_unavailable`, `llm_rate_limited`, `scope_too_large`, or `timed_out`. It is held in the process (`_ZB_ABORT_REASON`) and written into the sentinel `${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal`, which still crosses subshells and env scrubs (ADR-024). The first recorded abort wins. An empty sentinel reads as `sigint`. The run-level watchdog writes `timed_out` before sending SIGTERM to the process group; first-wins preserves `timed_out` over the `sigterm` that the runner's signal trap would otherwise record.
 - **The helpers return 0 or 1.** `_zbuild_abort <word>` records and returns 1; `_zbuild_abort_reason` reads the word back (from the sentinel when this process has none); `_zbuild_check_abort` is 1 when an abort is recorded; `_zbuild_propagate_abort <rc>` is 1 only when the child failed *and* an abort is recorded. `_zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel [word]` records (default `sigint`); disarming clears both channels.
 - **Every signal handler records the word:** the runner's (`_runner_signal_trap`), the cycle's (`_cycle_on_signal`) and the parallel group's (`_parallel_on_signal`). An `abort_when` match records `cycle_abort`; an unavailable model records `llm_unavailable` / `llm_rate_limited`.
 - **The runner ends on the word**, in one place (`_runner_end_on_abort`): `sigint` / `sigterm` / `cycle_abort` → status `interrupted`; `llm_unavailable` / `llm_rate_limited` / `scope_too_large` → status `aborted`. `pipeline.aborted` carries the word as its reason. The process exits 1 — the signal is in that reason, not in 130 or 143.
@@ -380,6 +380,10 @@ The dispatch-site contract is unchanged in shape: pre-flight `_zbuild_check_abor
 - Cleanup contract (the EXIT trap clears the sentinel; `pipeline.aborted reason=sigint` on Ctrl-C) → `tests/integration/full-pipeline-sigint-test.sh`
 - SIGTERM extension (`reason=sigterm`) → `tests/integration/sigterm-aborts-pipeline-test.sh`

+engine must enforce its own ceiling.

+**§11 — run-level wall-clock limit.**
+

+  `scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh`) using this precedence order:
+  1. Template `max_run_s:` key (top-level YAML) — read by `template_max_run_s()` in

+  2. `ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S` environment variable.
+  3. Engine default: **20700 seconds** (≈ 5 h 45 m).

+  disposition: the runner exits 1 before any stage runs.

+  `TRAVIS`, `CIRCLECI`, `RUNNER_OS`, or similar variables appears in the limit-resolution

+  sleeps for the resolved limit, writes `timed_out` to the abort sentinel

@@ -0,0 +1,161 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Integration: resumed run after timed_out uses a fresh watchdog (#1944)
+#
+# SPEC-4 [code]: a run resumed after a timed_out end is not stopped
+#   immediately — its watchdog is armed from the resumed run's wall-clock
+#   start, not the original run's.
+#
+# Phases:
+#   P1 (unit):        get_resume_recommendation(timed_out) = manual_resume_only;
+#                     not auto_resume and not fresh_start.
+#   P2 (unit):        _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined in stage-limits.sh
+#                     — the function that arms the watchdog on every invocation,
+#                     including --resume. Absent before the implementation.
+#   P3 (integration): a run resumed (--force) after a timed_out state with a
+#                     generous max_run_s completes normally — not stopped
+#                     immediately, proving the watchdog was armed from the
+#                     resumed run's wall-clock start.
+#
+# Why the test fails before implementation:
+#   P1: get_resume_recommendation has no timed_out case; the `*` catch-all
+#       returns fresh_start, not manual_resume_only. The assert_eq fails.
+#   P2: _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is not yet defined. The assert_fail fires.
+#   P3: passes even before implementation (no watchdog → run completes
+#       normally), but the earlier failures already cause the test to exit
+#       non-zero.
+set -uo pipefail
+
+SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
+
+# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
+source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
+# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
+source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
+
+print_test_header "resume-after-run-timeout: watchdog armed from resumed run's wall-clock start (#1944 SPEC-4)"
+setup_test_env "resume-after-run-timeout"
+
+# ─── P1: get_resume_recommendation returns manual_resume_only for timed_out ──
+print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-4] P1: get_resume_recommendation(timed_out) = manual_resume_only"
+
+# shellcheck source=../../core/state/resume.sh
+source "$REPO_ROOT/core/state/resume.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
+
+P1_STATE="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p1-timed-out-state.json"
+jq -n \
+    --arg now "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
+    '{schema_version:1, run_id:"test-run-timed-out", issue:0,
+      status:"timed_out", stage_statuses:{}, current_iteration:0,
+      self_heal_count:{}, scope_manifest_hash:"", cost_ledger_pointer:0,
+      claim_lease_id:"", plugin_state:{}, updated_at:$now}' \
+    > "$P1_STATE"
+
+if declare -F get_resume_recommendation >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    _p1_rec="$(get_resume_recommendation "$P1_STATE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
+    # Must be manual_resume_only — not fresh_start (the `*` catch-all before
+    # implementation) and not auto_resume (which would silently re-run it).
+    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-4] P1: get_resume_recommendation(timed_out) = manual_resume_only" \
+        "manual_resume_only" "$_p1_rec"
+else
+    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-4] P1: get_resume_recommendation is defined" \
+        "function not found after sourcing core/state/resume.sh"
+fi
+
+# ─── P2: _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined ───────────────────────────────
+print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-4] P2: _runner_resolve_run_limit_s defined (watchdog arms on every invocation)"
+
+# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh
+source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
+
+if declare -F _runner_resolve_run_limit_s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-4] P2: _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined in stage-limits.sh"
+else
+    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-4] P2: _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined in stage-limits.sh" \
+        "function not found — the watchdog cannot be armed on resume without it"
+fi
+
+# ─── P3: resumed run with generous limit completes — not stopped immediately ─
+print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-4] P3: resumed run completes normally with generous max_run_s"
+
+export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
+export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"
+export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
+export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
+export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn
+export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
+export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
+export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
+mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR" "$HOME/.zbuild"
+printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"
+
+# Quick-completing plugin (no sleep) — the resumed run's stage completes fast
+mock_plugin_factory "resume-stage" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
+
+# Overlay repo with a single-stage template
+RESUME_OVERLAY="$(setup_git_temp_repo resume-after-timeout)"
+mkdir -p "$RESUME_OVERLAY/.zbuild/templates"
+cat > "$RESUME_OVERLAY/.zbuild/templates/resume-timeout.yaml" <<'EOF'
+id: resume-timeout
+extends: simple
+stages:
+  - id: resume-stage
+    gate: auto
+    io:
+      destinations: [file]
+      tail_lines: 50
+EOF
+(cd "$RESUME_OVERLAY" && git add .zbuild && git commit -q -m "add resume-timeout template") \
+    >/dev/null 2>&1
+
+# Seed the state dir with a timed_out state, as if a previous run timed out.
+# The resumed run must arm its OWN watchdog from ITS wall-clock start, not
+# from the original run's start. With max_run_s=30 the new run has 30 s —
+# far more than the fast stage needs — so it must NOT be stopped immediately.
+RESUME_STATE_FILE="$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
+jq -n \
+    --arg now "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
+    '{schema_version:1, run_id:"prev-timed-out-run", issue:0,
+      status:"timed_out", stage_statuses:{}, current_iteration:0,
+      self_heal_count:{}, scope_manifest_hash:"", cost_ledger_pointer:0,
+      claim_lease_id:"", plugin_state:{}, updated_at:$now}' \
+    > "$RESUME_STATE_FILE"
+
+export ZBUILD_STATE_FILE="$RESUME_STATE_FILE"
+
+set +e
+( cd "$RESUME_OVERLAY" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=30 bash "$RUNNER" \
+    --template resume-timeout --goal "resume-after-timeout test p3" \
+    --resume --force ) \
+    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p3.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p3.stderr"
+_p3_rc=$?
+set -e
+
+# The resumed run must NOT end with timed_out — the fresh watchdog has
+# 30 s, and the stage completes in < 5 s.
+if [[ -f "$RESUME_STATE_FILE" ]]; then
+    _p3_status="$(jq -r '.status // empty' "$RESUME_STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
+    if [[ "$_p3_status" == "timed_out" ]]; then
+        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-4] P3: resumed run did not time out (watchdog is fresh)" \
+            "pipeline status is still timed_out — watchdog may have fired immediately"
+    else
+        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-4] P3: resumed run did not time out (status=$_p3_status)"
+    fi
+else
+    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-4] P3: pipeline-state.json accessible after resumed run" \
+        "state file not found: $RESUME_STATE_FILE"
+fi
+
+# No pipeline.end event with status=timed_out in the resumed run's events
+if [[ -f "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
+    _p3_to_events="$(jq -r \
+        'select(.type=="pipeline.end" and .data.status=="timed_out") | .type' \
+        "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ' || echo 0)"
+    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-4] P3: no pipeline.end/timed_out event in resumed run" \
+        "0" "$_p3_to_events"
+fi
+
+cleanup_test_env
+print_test_results
+exit $((FAIL > 0))

+id: limit-single
+extends: simple
+stages:
+  - id: intake
+    gate: auto
+    io:
+      destinations: [file]
+      tail_lines: 50
+EOF
+
+STAGE_MARKER="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/stage-ran-marker"
+cat > "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
+intake_run() {
+    : > "${STAGE_MARKER}"

+    return 0
+}
+PLUG
+
+set +e
+ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S="not-a-number" \
+( cd "$MISCFG_OVERLAY" && bash "$RUNNER" --template limit-single --goal "test misconfigured limit" ) \

+_miscfg_rc=$?
+set -e
+
+assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] invalid ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S → runner exits non-zero" "1" "$_miscfg_rc"

+    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] stage did not run when limit is misconfigured" \

+else
+    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-2] stage did not run when limit is misconfigured"

+    if grep -q "run-limit-precedence-test\|run-timed-out-test\|run-watchdog-clean-exit-test\|resume-after-run-timeout-test" \

+            "no run-limit test referenced in ADR-054 ## Enforced by"
+    fi
+fi
+
+print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-6] config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt does not list ADR-054-stage-contract.md"
+BASELINE="$REPO_ROOT/config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt"
+
+if [[ ! -f "$BASELINE" ]]; then
+    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-6] adr-enforcement-baseline.txt exists" "not found: $BASELINE"
+else
+    if grep -q 'ADR-054-stage-contract\.md' "$BASELINE" 2>/dev/null; then
+        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-6] ADR-054-stage-contract.md removed from baseline" \
+            "still listed in config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt"
+    else
+        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-6] ADR-054-stage-contract.md removed from baseline"
+    fi
+fi
+
+cleanup_test_env
+print_test_results

+print_test_results

_runner_abort_trap() {
        # ADR-054 §11 (#1944): disarm the watchdog before dispatching always-run
        # stages — it has already done its work (or was never needed on this path).
        # SIGKILL (not TERM): the watchdog has `trap '' TERM` so TERM would be
        # ignored and `wait` would block until the full sleep expires. SIGKILL
        # cannot be caught or ignored, so the wait returns immediately.
        kill -KILL "${_RUNNER_WATCHDOG_PID:-0}" 2>/dev/null || true
        wait "${_RUNNER_WATCHDOG_PID:-0}" 2>/dev/null || true
        # #1829: free live resources first, while the state file and the
        # process tree are still intact.
        _runner_dispatch_always_run
        # #1688: release the issue lock EXPLICITLY. Relying on process death is
        # not enough — a flock belongs to the open file description, which every
        # child inherits, so one lingering child would keep the issue locked
        # after this run is gone. Released after the always-run stages, which
        # still belong to this run.
        if declare -F zbuild_issue_lock_release >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            zbuild_issue_lock_release || true
        fi
        if declare -F zbuild_run_cap_release >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            zbuild_run_cap_release || true
        fi
        # ADR-054 §11 (#1944): capture the abort word BEFORE disarming the
        # sentinel — _zbuild_disarm_abort_sentinel clears both _ZB_ABORT_REASON
        # and the sentinel file. _RUNNER_ABORT_REASON is set by _runner_signal_trap
        # using first-wins semantics: if the watchdog wrote `timed_out` before the
        # signal fired, _runner_signal_trap's _zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel call saw it
        # and set _RUNNER_ABORT_REASON="timed_out". This survives the disarm.
        local _at_abort_word; _at_abort_word="${_RUNNER_ABORT_REASON:-}"
        # ADR-025 (Wave 15-B #684): the sentinel must be cleared on EVERY
        # exit path — clean end, normal failure, or abort — so a follow-on
        # zbuild invocation in the same state_dir never sees a stale
        # signal. Runs BEFORE the short-circuit because the
        # `_runner_ended=true` path is the common case (every successful
        # run hits it) and that path also needs the cleanup.
        _zbuild_disarm_abort_sentinel
        # Best-effort: drop THIS run's own lock siblings so a killed run does
        # not leave a stale .lock behind. flock releases on fd close at process
        # death regardless, but the on-disk lock FILE would otherwise linger;
        # this is belt-and-suspenders to the authoritative --no-resume startup
        # clear (the trap may be deferred behind a foreground `wait`, #run-hygiene).
        if [[ -n "${_runner_state_file:-}" ]]; then
            local _rd; _rd="$(dirname "$_runner_state_file")"
            rm -f "$_runner_state_file.lock" "$_rd/events.jsonl.lock" \
                  "$_rd/events.db.lock" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
        # #2131: the normal path — pipeline.end and the always-run stages are
        # on disk; the sidecar renders them in its final PATCH, then goes.
        if [[ "$_runner_ended" == "true" ]]; then _runner_status_comment_reap; return 0; fi
        if [[ "${_at_abort_word:-}" == "timed_out" ]]; then
            if ! _set_pipeline_status "$_runner_state_file" "timed_out" 2>/dev/null; then
                eb_emit_event "pipeline.state.error" \
                    "run_id=$_runner_run_id" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
                    "reason=abort_trap_set_status_failed" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
            eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=timed_out" \
                "stage=${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" \
                "limit_s=${_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S:-}" \
                "run_id=$_runner_run_id" "issue=$_runner_issue" 2>/dev/null || true
            ( _render_pipeline_end "timed_out" ) || true
